entries.title: Azuremyst Isle
body: A green, misty island of blue-leaved forest off the western coast of Kalimdor, near Darkshore. Night elves lived here long ago and left ruins along its shores; furbolgs, owlkin and murlocs have had it largely to themselves since.

That changed when the Exodar fell out of the sky. The vast crystal vessel of the draenei crashed on the island's north-western side, scattering pieces of itself across the forests and lakes. The survivors, led by the Prophet Velen, have made the wreck their city and Azuremyst their new home, after ten lifetimes of fleeing the Burning Legion.

The crash was not gentle on the land. Fallen crystals are poisoning water and twisting animals, blood elves who followed the draenei from Outland are hunting them still, and the island's older peoples are not all sure what to make of the newcomers.
sources: creature 17116 gossip (ten lifetimes spent fleeing the Legion)
quest 9633 offer text (isles once inhabited by night elves)
pre-Cataclysm lore: the Exodar's flight from Outland and crash

entries.title: Ammen Vale
body: A small isle off the eastern tip of Azuremyst, separated from the larger island by the Crystalbrook River. A broken section of the Exodar came down here, and the draenei who woke inside it had no idea at first whether anyone else had survived.

The vale is pretty and badly hurt. The crash fouled its lake and fields, mutated the plants and beasts that live there, and scattered injured draenei, still glowing red from the ship's irradiated crystals, among the trees. Blood elf scouts were watching from the ridge almost before the survivors could stand.
sources: quest 9313 description (path west off this tiny isle across the Crystalbrook River)

entries.title: The Crash Site
body: The wrecked section of the Exodar at the heart of Ammen Vale. Its suspension pods held sleeping draenei, some of them for weeks, and only those who were in this part of the ship came out alive.

The survivors set to work at once. Proenitus and the priest Zalduun refilled the healing crystals with the blood of vale moths, regretting every death; Botanist Taerix and her apprentices studied the poisoned plants; Vindicator Aldar organised the defence; and Technician Zhanaa pieced together a holographic emitter from salvage until it could reach the draenei at Azure Watch.

entries.title: Silverline Lake
body: The lake at the south of Ammen Vale. One of the Exodar's power crystals plunged into it during the crash and has been leaking into the water ever since, poisoning the lake and spreading strange growths and mutations across the vale.
Botanist Taerix brewed a neutralising agent that was scattered over the crystal, and it worked, at least for a time. She would far rather have the crystal lifted out of the lake altogether.

entries.title: Nestlewood
body: Wooded hills and thickets in the south-east of Ammen Vale, home to the Nestlewood owlkin. Much of the ship's salvage landed here, and the owlkin carried off pieces of it before the draenei could reach them.

Some of the owlkin were maddened by the crash's poison and had to be killed. The draenei were unwilling to wipe out the rest, so Taerix prepared an inoculating crystal to protect the healthy ones, and the survivors could search for spare parts without a war on their hands.

entries.title: Shadow Ridge
body: A ridge on the far side of Silverline Lake, in the south-west of Ammen Vale. Draenei scouts reported strange activity up there, and one of them, Tolaan, did not come back.

He was found badly wounded. Blood elves had made camp on the ridge under a surveyor named Candress, and their plans showed that they had followed the draenei to Azeroth. Vindicator Aldar's first reaction was to wish them wiped from existence; his second was to apologise for saying it.

entries.title: Azure Watch
body: A draenei outpost on the road west of the Crystalbrook, one of two forward bases of the Hand of Argus. Survivors who stagger in from the wreckage find a bed with Caregiver Chellan, and the healers here are never short of patients.

Exarch Menelaous commands it. Around him the outpost has filled with useful people: the hunter Acteon, the fisher Diktynna down at the river, an alchemist and an anchorite, and a Stillpine furbolg named Arugoo. Beside them stands a carved furbolg totem that the cryptographer Aurren believes holds the key to the Stillpine language.
sources: quest 9694 description (two forward bases of the Hand of Argus)

entries.title: Moongraze Woods
body: Open woodland south of Azure Watch, grazed by herds of moongraze stags. Their tender meat has become a staple of the outpost.

The draenei hunters took to them quickly. The stags look much like the talbuk of Draenor, which were the greatest prey of draenei hunters back home, and the tougher bucks further north are prized for their hides.

entries.title: Odesyus' Landing
body: A camp on Azuremyst's southern shore, where the two ships of Admiral Odesyus of Alliance Naval Command were forced to put in. Goblin stowaways had robbed the ships of their navigation gear and vanished into the forest.

The landing has a varied crew. Its cook, "Cookie" McWeaksauce, is a reformed pirate who practises his pirate talk so as not to lose it; the night elf priestess Kyleen Il'dinare has come to look after her people's old lands; and Adamant Ironheart, retired from Ironforge's elite guard, is digging for night elf relics for the Explorers' League.

entries.title: Geezle's Camp
body: A Venture Company camp in the woods east of Odesyus' Landing, run by a goblin named Geezle. Its people came ashore hidden in the admiral's own holds.

Orders from Mogul Razdunk, found rolled up in the stolen navigation map, explained their purpose: to strip-mine the Exodar's crystal wreckage from the island, then seize the Alliance ships to carry the haul away. Somebody had told them exactly where the ships would go.
sources: creatures 17278 Venture Co. Saboteur, 17279 Venture Co. Gemologist

entries.title: Traitor's Cove
body: A quiet cove on the south-western coast. When a naga flag is raised on the shore, it means a meeting has been arranged there.

The cove took its name from one such meeting. Geezle came to report to his contact, and an observer hidden in a hollow tree and a pile of leaves saw who that contact was: Engineer "Spark" Overgrind, a gnome of Admiral Odesyus' own expedition.

entries.title: Wrathscale Point
body: The ruins of an ancient night elf city on Azuremyst's south-western shore, now overrun by naga of the Wrathscale. Priestess Kyleen believes the spirits of the dead there are restless, and treats the naga as an insult to her ancestors.

The naga are also a threat. A tablet found in the ruins pointed to their leader, Warlord Sriss'tiz, who was hiding in the sea cave of Tides' Hollow along the western coast and preparing an invasion. The Explorers' League, meanwhile, would like whatever relics the naga leave lying around.

entries.title: Bristlelimb Village
body: A furbolg den in the south-western forest, reached by the old elven road. It belongs to the Bristlelimb tribe, enemies of the Stillpine.
The Bristlelimb raided the Stillpine while their guard was down and carried off their young. The captives are kept in cages around the village, and the Bristlelimb carry the keys.

entries.title: Stillpine Hold
body: The cave home of the Stillpine furbolgs in northern Azuremyst. After the crystal storm, wildkin who had once been the tribe's allies turned on them, drove them from the hold and moved in, bringing with them a beast out of furbolg legend, the Kurken.

The Stillpine camp outside the entrance with a defensive line built to stop anything that comes out. Inside, near the water the tribe drinks, a blood-red crystal from the Exodar is slowly dissolving into the cave's pool.

entries.title: Silting Shore
body: The beach west of Stillpine Hold, home to the Siltfin murlocs. The Stillpine had always got on uneasily with them; lately the murlocs have grown bold enough to raid the tribe's food stores.
Gurf the Brave of the Stillpine came off worst. A dark murloc named Murgurgula kicked him, spat on him and went off with a patch of his fur, which the murloc now wears between his toes.

entries.title: Menagerie Wreckage
body: Debris from the Exodar east of the road near Stillpine Hold. The ship carried living specimens from Outland, and here some of them escaped.

The furbolgs had never seen anything like the ravagers that now prowl the wreck, insect-like predators that ambushed the hunter Moordo and his brother. Some of the Stillpine took them for beasts of the apocalypse.
sources: quest 9634 description (Exodar carried Outland specimens including ravagers)

entries.title: Silvermyst Isle
body: A small island off Azuremyst's south-western coast, where the night elf fisherman Cowlen lived with his wife Thalrisa and daughter Magwin among the owlbeasts.

The peace ended suddenly. Owlkin and murlocs stormed the beach, Cowlen's home was razed and his boat sunk, and he believes his family was devoured. He sits by the docks on the island's south-east side, waiting for someone to bring back what is left of them.

entries.title: Exarch Menelaous
body: The commander of Azure Watch. He looks at the wrecked Exodar and wonders that anyone survived it, and he believes, as the Prophet does, that this world is where the draenei will finally stop running. He has said he is ready to die here.

Menelaous does not hide from bad news. When a crystal shard turned up in the belly of a nightstalker, he admitted the draenei had ignored early reports of crystal in the river, and ordered the infected beasts culled before the contamination could spread.

entries.title: Admiral Odesyus
body: A human admiral of Alliance Naval Command, whose two ships were driven to Azuremyst by goblin stowaways. He is embarrassed by the whole affair and not at all embarrassed by his plan to fix it, which involved disguising a volunteer as a tree.

Odesyus suspected a traitor from the moment he read the Venture Company's orders, and trusted none of his own crew until he knew who it was. Since then he has become a friend of the draenei, and passes on warnings from stranger sources, including the ghost of a long-dead sea captain.
sources: quest 9751 description (Edward Hanes appeared in his tent)
quest 9671 offer text (a human admiral from Azuremyst)

entries.title: Priestess Kyleen Il'dinare
body: A night elf priestess of Elune travelling with Odesyus' expedition. She believes fate brought them to Azuremyst, the land of her ancestors, and has set herself to cleansing its ruins of naga.

She does not trust the draenei. To her eyes they look too much like the eredar, the race of Archimonde, who nearly destroyed her people. The Prophet Velen foresaw exactly this: that the draenei's new allies would ask them to answer for the sins of their fathers. Kyleen admits her doubts may fade in time, and deeds have begun to change her mind.

entries.title: Engineer "Spark" Overgrind
body: A gnome engineer who sailed with Odesyus' expedition as an envoy of High Tinker Mekkatorque. He is always too busy to talk.

He was busy with treason. Spark was the one who told the Venture Company where the Alliance ships would be, and letters on him show that he answered to Kael'thas Sunstrider himself, who wanted the gnome's skills to repair the Exodar once his forces had taken it back. That a high-ranking envoy of the Alliance could be bought made the admiral wonder how many others might be.

entries.title: Cowlen and Magwin
body: Cowlen is a night elf fisherman of Silvermyst Isle who lost everything when the island's creatures turned on his family. He does not want revenge, only to bury his dead properly, and in his worst moments he has asked strangers to end his life for him.

His daughter Magwin was not dead. She escaped the attack, and weeks later was still trying to make her way home through the forest. Their reunion moved Cowlen to give away a family heirloom, a night elf token of friendship and trust.

entries.title: Kurz the Revelator
body: The seer of the Stillpine tribe. Several months ago Kurz began to see dark omens: the gods would shatter the land and turn friend and foe alike against the furbolgs.
His visions also promised a saviour, a hero not of Stillpine blood. Kurz greets outsiders who have helped his people as the Promised One, and in his visions it is that hero who kills the Kurken.

entries.title: The Fall of the Exodar
body: The Exodar was never a draenei ship. It was a vessel of the naaru from Tempest Keep, and when Velen's people escaped Outland in it, Kael'thas Sunstrider counted it as stolen from him. Blood elves fought the draenei aboard, and the ship came down in pieces on the Azuremyst Isles.

The draenei were scattered: survivors in the wreck of Ammen Vale, others at Azure Watch and Blood Watch, and many more lost. The blood elves survived too. Letters taken from Kael'thas' agents show that an eredar agent of his master sent him the crash site, and that he means to retake the ship and kill every draenei on the isles.
sources: page text 2919-2920 (Traitor's Communication: they have stolen MY vessel)
quest 9694 description (blood elves battling on the Exodar survived the crash)
pre-Cataclysm lore: the naaru and Tempest Keep, the draenei escape from Outland

entries.title: Poisoned Crystals
body: The Exodar ran on crystals, and when it broke up they fell everywhere: into Silverline Lake, into the Crystalbrook, into the caves of the Stillpine. Irradiated and cracked, they have been leaking into the water ever since.

Plants and animals that drink it change. Lashers mutate, owlkin and wildkin turn on old friends, and nightstalkers are found with shards in their stomachs. The draenei admit they ignored the first signs, and are now trying to stop the damage before it spreads further across the islands.

entries.title: The Prophecy of Akida
body: The Stillpine furbolgs write their language on carved totems marked with owls, bears, wolves and stags. Each totem points the way to the next, and together they tell the tribe's history and its prophecies. The draenei learned to read them from the totem at Azure Watch.

The last totems record a war with the Bristlelimb tribe, and a prophecy that a hero not of furbolg blood would rise to save the Stillpine. When an outsider freed the Stillpine captives, killed the Kurken and cleared the hold, the tribe declared the prophecy fulfilled, and High Chief Stillpine promised the draenei the tribe's aid whenever they ask.

entries.title: The Blood Elves on the Isles
body: The blood elves who followed the Exodar are not hiding. Scouts were surveying Ammen Vale soon after the crash, and a ledger taken from blood elf bandits showed a bounty paid for every dead draenei.

Their reach goes further than swords. Through goblins and a bought gnome, Kael'thas had a spy inside an Alliance expedition, and the draenei learned they had been watched far longer than they knew. Exarch Menelaous sent every warning on to Velen, and the Hand of Argus prepared for the fight on Bloodmyst.
